lastText: File ClosedThe Alliance That HeldMajor VictoryThe War Cabinet and Chiefs of Staff, 1939–1945End of hostilities: NOVEMBER 1945 (PROJECTED) · filed out of sequence, pages missingImmediate AftermathVictory in Europe arrives around November 1945: ██████ than the historical May 1945, the █████ of caution at the moments this campaign offered a faster, ███████ road instead. The campaign reaches its end having spent more Western Allied lives than the historical record: the price of the bolder, more aggressive road at several of this campaign's genuine forks. Market Garden's reach for Arnhem was ██████ back before it happened rather than mourned after: Browning's private reservation taken seriously instead of overruled. Yalta was met with a truly united Anglo-American front on Poland: the option the historical conference never had, purchased by two years of managed alliance, extracting language Stalin had to openly repudiate rather than quietly reinterpret. Coalition Cohesion held solid across the war's hardest disagreements: the Western partnership that would anchor NATO within a few years was, on this path, unusually strong from the very start.
